# Native app-only source commands

The maintained `linux/install.sh` and `linux/uninstall.sh` now prepare an optimized native bundle and invoke the same Rust install/removal transactions used by packaged applications. `linux/build-native.sh` explicitly builds the nine production executables and the unshipped package builder with locked dependencies. The builder defaults to its own executable directory when no binary directory is supplied, so a configured Cargo target cannot accidentally select old binaries from a guessed `release/` path. The existing explicit-directory package interface remains available.

Build artifacts use `tmp/native-build` unless `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is supplied. Relative Cargo cache/toolchain/target paths resolve against the caller before changing to the source root. Each source command owns a fresh private bundle under the checkout's `tmp/`; it removes that bundle after success or failure. No compiler failure falls back to Python. Build prerequisites and the distinction between source commands and compiler-free installed commands are documented in [CONTRIBUTING](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md#local-setup).

The coordinator isolates the compiler process group, forwards cancellation and waits before removing its temporary payload. The native installer remains in the caller's terminal session and foreground group, with stdin preserved, so an existing privileged input-service migration can authenticate. Cancellation targets that owned native child; its existing transaction owns its subprocesses and rollback. Neither coordinator signals the user's terminal group.

## Independent source-boundary checks

`source_checkout_installs_upgrades_and_removes_without_python` runs the actual maintained source commands in a guarded private prefix. A positive absolute `/usr/bin/python3` trap proves the interpreter boundary is observable. Two complete source builds install and upgrade the actual production bundle; the public launcher matches the immutable v1.6.0 CLI, the receipt identifies Rust, and the upgrade preserves the complete installed/user snapshot. A real compiler process returning 73 leaves that snapshot unchanged. A blocked compiler receives cancellation through the public source command; the command exits 143, its compiler is gone and all installed/user bytes remain. Actual source removal preserves an unrelated user file. The installed payload is copied aside before removal for the existing resident and package comparisons.

`legacy::source_upgrade_keeps_the_authentication_terminal` runs the source installer through a real private pseudo-terminal. Its controlled `sudo -v` endpoint must receive terminal stdin and read a synthetic confirmation from `/dev/tty`; no password or privileged operation is performed. Existing mount/device-inode guards remain on every service mutation. The actual migration then installs Rust, retires the old owned service and preserves enabled/active state. This protects a source-coordinator boundary that direct native-installer tests cannot reach.

The former source installer fails the first check with interpreter-trap status 99 in `tmp/native-source-before.log`. The first native coordinator fails terminal authentication with status 65 in `tmp/native-source-terminal-before.log`, evidence `tmp/native-source-terminal-before-evidence/session.U6b1IA/`. Keeping the installer in its caller's terminal repairs that failure. Both checks pass in `tmp/native-source-acceptance.log`, evidence `tmp/native-source-acceptance-evidence/session.zfNida/`, with Python and external networking blocked. These are cached native builds on the existing development machine, not clean-distribution dependency provisioning.

## Retired implementation and test ownership

Before removal, the complete old installer/remover, migration implementation, launcher template, related tests/callers and history were reviewed. The former public source installer was the only production caller of `linux/migrate_legacy.py`; it also rendered `linux/resources/mluva.in`. Both paths become obsolete when source installation delegates to the independently verified native owners. Git retains the immutable released implementation at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`; no reference fixture or expected value is changed.

The removed tests protected real contracts. They are retired with their obsolete implementation, with the following stronger independent owners retained:

| Removed location and exact test names | Protected behavior and retained owner |
| --- | --- |
| `linux/tests/test_launcher.py`: `test_launcher_prefers_enabled_snapshot`, `test_launcher_uses_scoped_managed_profile_when_credential_is_missing`, `test_launcher_skips_available_managed_credentials`, `test_launcher_skips_scribe_secret_resolution_for_other_providers`; `linux/tests/test_managed_agent_launcher.py`: `test_agent_fallback_requests_only_elevenlabs_and_preserves_arguments` | Snapshot/scoped/agent priority, existing-key/provider bypass and argument retention. [Native managed startup](../../../mluva-gtk/tests/fixtures/launcher-evidence.md) compares 72 actual released invocations and three direct narration routes, including process identity, signals, settings tolerance and helper failures. The template-rendering test helpers and separate fallback test file are removed. |
| `linux/tests/test_launcher.py`: `test_uninstaller_removes_only_staged_application_files`, `test_uninstaller_refuses_an_unrecognized_application_directory` | Removal ownership, staged isolation and retained user data. [Native removal](uninstall-evidence.md) compares 39 released commands, six additional guards and actual complete-payload self-removal. |
| `linux/tests/test_launcher.py`: `test_installer_rejects_an_unrecognized_application_directory`, `test_installer_rejects_an_unsafe_live_xdg_root`, `test_installer_preserves_an_unrelated_canonical_command`, `test_installer_preserves_an_unrelated_helper_link`, `test_installer_rolls_back_a_failed_environment_sync`, `test_installer_replaces_a_complete_current_install` | Installation ownership, unsafe roots, unrelated commands, failed preparation and complete upgrade. [Native installation](install-evidence.md) compares nineteen released outcomes, nine complete-preservation cases, cancellation/concurrent ownership, six admission guards and actual bundle install/self-upgrade. The new source-boundary check additionally guards real compiler failure/cancellation before those transactions. |
| `linux/tests/test_legacy_migration.py`: `test_upgrade_preserves_state_and_retires_active_artifacts`, `test_failed_upgrade_restores_old_state_launchers_and_integrations`, `test_upgrade_conflicts_fail_before_mutation`, `test_gnome_preferences_keep_pins_and_drop_retired_altgr_helper`, `test_unrecognized_profile_is_never_printed`, `test_interrupted_upgrade_restores_the_previous_install`, `test_failed_system_service_start_restores_template_and_prior_state` | SQLite/audio/configuration retention, conflict and credential privacy, desktop preferences, interruption and service rollback. [Native migration](legacy-evidence.md) compares 34 actual released transactions, five additional service/ownership faults and complete-package migration/startup. The old migration test file and Python implementation are removed together. |

Relevant history includes `19c7579` (identity migration and backups), `59d0ff5` (guided local-model setup), `97d1007` (test/guard repairs), `2868c7a` (security fixes), `6ca78b1` (managed snapshot startup) and `3bf77f7` (combined repository installation). The risk is losing existing-state or credential behavior during source cutover, so validation exercises the public source commands and all retained transaction/removal/launcher owners. It does not replace those contracts with shell-text checks. Three tests remain in `linux/tests/test_launcher.py`: the development lockfile contract and both standalone `configure-secret-profile.sh` contracts, because those production entry points still exist.

## Regression evidence and remaining gates

`tmp/native-source-regression.log`, evidence `tmp/native-source-regression-evidence/session.N8xPGG/`, passes all eight existing installation/migration checks, all three removal checks and the 72-case managed-launcher comparison. Complete-payload checks use the retained source-built bundle. Its first resident comparison records a visible Commands window before accessibility content becomes observable. The observer previously waited a fixed 250 ms; it now waits, with the existing bounded deadline, for nonempty public accessibility content before comparing the entire unchanged snapshot. It does not wait for equality or change the application to satisfy the observer. The failed observation remains in that log.

The reviewed terminal regression, complete resident comparison and optimized package/archive check pass in `tmp/native-source-reviewed.log`, evidence `tmp/native-source-reviewed-evidence/session.Wgcpxr/`. Resident checks retain all 38 public states, thirteen actions and five CLI contracts, forwarding, cold synthetic-PCM Record/quit and three startup faults. The package comparison retains explicit-directory construction, checksum/notice validation, independent archive extraction, repeated-byte equality and destination protection. The source-built main executable is SHA-256 `472fa8e8503458189b2d62a2cbeed3def052ea0ce0522935ec58c3fe31966aca`. The final package archive is 17,272,563 bytes with SHA-256 `2ac434ad8706454a9a841345bb6b6aac03fb501deb4a0fd8c72b031cf2e94145`; repeated output matches. Its receipt is `dfcd3c8ab39696c0000de1bf1a2ed97c5e246afe0363be2079d571aeac9eb332`; the dependency inventory remains `77ac24e78a5344e914341c9c40163e196ebdc26558dcd0eeeb1136428c6ced6d`.

Final `cargo test --locked --workspace` passes **139 tests, zero failures and 63 ignored environment checks across 97 suites** in `tmp/native-source-final-workspace.log`. Affected ignored tests were explicitly run above. Strict all-target Clippy passes in `tmp/native-source-final-clippy.log`; formatting, diff and the full documented ShellCheck gate pass. `make linux-test` passes **598 tests**, Ruff and formatting for 167 files in `tmp/native-source-final-linux.log`; its existing PyGObject deprecation warning remains. The private-bus shortcut gate passes in `tmp/native-source-final-shortcut.log`. Compared with the prior checkpoint, production/tooling changes add 118 lines and remove 905; tests/support add 291 and remove 804. Those counts exclude documentation.

With the pinned compiler/cache and guarded desktop prerequisites available, run the source checks explicitly:

```sh
export CARGO_HOME="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}"
export RUSTUP_HOME="${RUSTUP_HOME:-$HOME/.rustup}"
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$PWD/tmp/native-build}"
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/native-source-check -- \
  cargo test --locked -p mluva-install --test install source_ -- \
  --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

The session's `install-source/source-built-bundle` file names the retained actual payload. Pass that path as `MLUVA_TEST_NATIVE_BUNDLE` to the existing install/removal/resident comparisons; set `MLUVA_TEST_NATIVE_NARRATION` to its `bin/mluva-narrate` for the managed-launcher comparison. Run isolated sessions sequentially. The ordinary workspace deliberately ignores these checks rather than opening a user's desktop.

Root source dependency/widget provisioning, the remaining Make/development commands and Python tooling still need conversion. Whole-application workflows, private Wayland selection/widget upgrade, broader target/theme/scale acceptance, physical keys/microphone and remaining performance measurements stay open. No whole-workflow parity row is promoted. The installed app and widget remain the verified 1.6.0 release, with no user-prefix, desktop, microphone, clipboard, credential or real-service changes.
